messages:
PagerBot: [PAGE] P1 - GPU queue growth detected for cluster acme-prod (private-vpc/us-west2). Pending GPU pods: 1,820; token backlog increasing. Autoscaler attempted but cluster node count stuck at 2. Paging SREs now.
Elena (SRE): Oncall ack, looking. Can someone drop the autoscaler logs and pending pod list?
Jordan (Infra): acme-prod. Quick snapshot: kube-autoscaler reports repeated scaleUp retries and a couple of rejections. Early logs show 'scaleUp rejected: reached maxSize for pool acme-gpu (4)'. Also saw intermittent image pull errors earlier.
Carol (Eng): Rolling in. Can you paste `kubectl get pods --field-selector=status.phase==Pending -n acme-prod | wc -l` and a sample `kubectl describe pod`?
Jordan (Infra): sample outputs below:
```
$ kubectl get pods -n acme-prod | grep Pending | wc -l
1820
$ kubectl describe pod batch-heavy-xyz -n acme-jobs
Status: Pending
Events:
  Type    Reason             Age   From               Message
  ----    ------             ----  ----               -------
  Warning FailedScheduling   3m    default-scheduler  0/12 nodes are available: 12 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu
```
Elena (SRE): So nodes exist but no GPU capacity. Autoscaler says pool maxed out and cloud provider not allocating more: suspect pool config + customer quota/AMI limits.
Maya (Support): Impact from support: Acme is seeing inference timeouts and elevated 5xx rates in their prod API. Customer Ops: "~30% error rate spike, we're getting end-user alerts".
Customer Ops (Acme Inc): Confirming. Workloads are production tuning jobs; we have critical customers affected. Please advise ETA.
Carol (Eng): Two vectors: 1) runaway job requests too many GPUs (check pod spec), 2) autoscaler pool limits / node provisioning blocked by image or instance type availability.
Jordan (Infra): Checked ASG/scale pool: acme-gpu pool is configured max=4, min=2. We see scaling attempts but max reached. Cloud provider logs show: `InsufficientInstanceCapacity: no capacity for g5-type in us-west2` and a couple `InstanceLimitExceeded` for the customer's account.
Elena (SRE): OK. Short term mitigations: A) bump pool max to 8 (if provider allows), B) evict/kill noncritical batch jobs, C) create temporary fallback pool with a compatible GPU type. Which we can do manually.
Maya (Support): Customer acceptance check: Will a restart/evict of the big job cause data loss? They say the jobs are restartable but take hours.
Carol (Eng): There's a particular job `batch-heavy-xyz` requesting 160 GPUs via a single pod (looks like a mis-submit). We should isolate/evict that one to free scheduler pressure.
Elena (SRE): Agreed. I'll evict that pod and scale a temporary pool. Commands I'm running now:
```
# evict runaway pod
kubectl delete pod batch-heavy-xyz -n acme-jobs --grace-period=0 --force
# scale pool
redwoodctl pools update --cluster acme-prod --pool acme-gpu --max 8
# create fallback pool
redwoodctl pools create --cluster acme-prod --name acme-gpu-compat --instance-type g4dn.xlarge --count 2 --labels fallback=true
```
deploy-bot: pool update job queued (job id: job-8792). Fallback pool creation started. ETA ~5-8m.
Jordan (Infra): Noted cloud provider returned a short quota error for the customer's project; opened request for temporary quota bump but not immediate. Fallback pool uses different instance type and should avoid that quota.
Maya (Support): Let me ping Acme slack: "we are evicting a heavy job and standing up fallback nodes, will update in 10m" :thumbsup:.
Customer Ops (Acme Inc): Please confirm we won't evict anything that holds critical state. The job is checkpointed every 30m. We prefer eviction over indefinite backlog.
Elena (SRE): Understood. Proceeding with eviction now (grace 0 to speed scheduling).
Elena (SRE): Eviction done. Confirmed pods moved from Pending -> Terminating for that job, new pending count down to ~1620.
deploy-bot: fallback pool acme-gpu-compat created, 2 nodes provisioning.
Jordan (Infra): New nodes registered to cluster, kubelet ready on both. Scheduler started placing smaller GPU pods on fallback nodes. Pending count down to 410.
Carol (Eng): Good. Still seeing some head-of-line blocking from large-request pods; recommend adding a pod-queue priority class or set a quota to prevent single pods hogging entire pool.
Elena (SRE): Agreed, will apply a temporary LimitRange and a quota to the acme-jobs ns to cap requests. Running:
```
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: temp-gpu-limits
  namespace: acme-jobs
spec:
  limits:
  - type: Pod
    max:
      nvidia.com/gpu: "8"
EOF
```
Maya (Support): Customer update sent: "We've evicted a runaway job and added temporary nodes; errors should reduce over next 10m."
Customer Ops (Acme Inc): Seeing error rate drop. Thank you. Let us know if you need us to stop any job.
Elena (SRE): Current status: Pending pods ~60, new nodes stabilized, request latency back to baseline for most traffic. Autoscaler adjustments persisted (max=8). Blocking issues: provider quota request pending, need to monitor for next 24h.
Jordan (Infra): Follow-ups: 1) Request permanent pool max increase or autoscaling policy change, 2) advise customer on submission validation to prevent single huge pod, 3) track cloud quota escalation.
Carol (Eng): I'll open a post-incident task to add admission webhook to reject >16 GPU single-pod requests and recommend job sharding.
Maya (Support): Impact summary for Acme: P1-ish customer-visible errors for ~22 minutes, now mitigated. Raising to CS to follow up on SLA.
Elena (SRE): Oncall handoff: I'm staying for 30m to confirm stability, then hand to night oncall. @night-oncall please monitor GPU queue, autoscaler events, and cloud quota ticket (internal id: cloud-req-4421).
PagerBot: Incident record created: INC-2410004321. Status: mitigated -> monitoring.
Elena (SRE): Closing thread for now, will update incident page with timeline and actions.
